doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Life in Riverdale and visiting Brazilian musicians
summary: The grounds and sculptures, the sledding story, and Brazilian musicians such as Jobim and Joao Gilberto coming via Don Payne.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And there were big sculptures on the property too that were part of the art.

The front gate is of a huge dog, this high, one on each side, and you walk through them and that’s the entrance to the grounds. There was a 350-year-old copper beech tree on the grounds, and up the hill was the Dodge estate, and that became, in the winter, a sledding hill, and it was a dangerous hill, because our drummer, who had been a paratrooper, he and I went sledding. And we’d go down this hill and you’d make a turn here go up around this one and go along this path, and he went over the path and he fell down over nine feet onto a driveway, and he said, “oh, it was just like a parachute jump.”

It was like heaven though, you know, because it was great for the kids, it was a great neighborhood for them to be in, and we just really enjoyed it for eleven years. Oh and all the Brazilians came there too because every time, at that time, when anybody was coming to New York from Brazil, all the musicians, they would come to our friend Don Payne’s house.
Because he had been in Brazil with Tony Bennett.

And they’d come to his house and he’d bring them over to our house, and we had several sessions with them playing in our dining room. And we met Antonio Carlos Jobim, we met Joao Gilberto, we met Carlos Lyra, Edu Lobo, and Astrud was married to Joao at the time, and they came over with their little child, and I mean we met all these people, it was great, just wonderful.
Boy you have had some angelic guidance along the way.
Well it seems that way, yeah. Thank you.
